transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today... I hope I'm not taking up too much of your schedule. 

Well, I'm here because... it's a bit embarrassing to admit at my age, to be honest. It's a bit silly, really, but I seem to have this... this reaction to bridges. The moment I realize that crossing one is completely unavoidable, I... well, my heart just starts pounding away. My hands get all damp on the steering wheel, or the armrest if someone else is driving, and I just get this terrible rush of fear before I'm even on the bridge itself. 

I know it sounds foolish for an old man to get so worked up over a simple drive, and I hate to make a fuss over it... am I making sense, Doctor? Is this the sort of thing you help people with?
Do you experience similar feelings of fear or panic in situations other than crossing bridges, or does this only happen specifically when you're about to cross a bridge?

Oh, no, no, it's really just the bridges. I don't want you to think I'm a complete nervous wreck about everything else, I promise I'm usually quite level-headed. It's just this one peculiar thing. 

I try to reason with myself, I really do. I know perfectly well that thousands of cars cross those bridges every single day without a hitch. I know the engineering is sound. But... well, when I see a high span on a map, or if I spot it looming up ahead through the windshield, I just can't help it. It feels to me as if the whole thing is waiting to drop away right under us. 

I know it sounds terribly foolish for a grown man to think that way... does that make any sense at all, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining myself properly for you.
Is your fear limited to certain types of bridges, like high ones or long ones, or does it happen with any bridge, even smaller or less imposing ones?

Well, I suppose... I mean, I don't want to sound completely unreasonable. A little stone bridge over a creek in a park, that's fine. I wouldn't even blink at that. It's really the... the larger ones that seem to give me trouble. 

The ones that go high up over the water, or the very long ones where you can't quite see the other side right away... those are the ones that really get to me. I try to avoid them if I can help it, taking the longer route just so I don't have to bother anyone with my silly nerves. But even the highway overpasses, if they're high enough, can make me a bit... uncomfortable. 

I know it's silly to differentiate between them, a bridge is a bridge, after all. I hope I'm not making things too complicated for you, Doctor. Is that the sort of detail you need?

When you're faced with crossing one of these bridges, do you ever feel like you're having a panic attack — like your chest tightens up, you can't catch your breath, or you feel like you're going to lose control?

Well, I... I wouldn't call it a panic attack, exactly. That sounds so dramatic, doesn't it? I don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart at the seams. 

I do get a bit tense, yes. My chest might feel a little tight, and... and perhaps I breathe a bit faster than usual. Sometimes I feel a little lightheaded if it's a particularly high span. But I try very hard to keep it together, especially if someone else is in the car. I'd hate to make a scene or frighten anyone. 

I just grip the handle above the door and close my eyes and wait for it to be over. It's terribly uncomfortable, but I wouldn't say I lose control. I try to be very good about it. Am I making sense, Doctor? I hope I'm not downplaying it too much if it's important for you to know.
Do you ever go out of your way to avoid routes that involve crossing bridges, even if it means taking a much longer or less convenient path?

Well, I... I suppose I do, yes. I try not to make a fuss about it, but... well, for over two years now, I've been rather careful about planning my errands and visits. I just map things out beforehand to... to steer clear of them, if I can. 

I don't want to sound like a burden to my family, but I have stopped going on our trips out to the San Juan Islands, and I gave up my theater nights in Seattle. It's just easier that way, you know? Less trouble for everyone if I just stay closer to home. 

And if I absolutely, positively must cross one... well, I need the whole route studied in advance. I have to get the timing just right, usually when there's less traffic, and... and I really need someone in the car with me. I just sit there feeling quite frightened the whole way across, holding on tight. 

I know it sounds like such a dreadful inconvenience, and I do apologize if it seems like I'm letting this get out of hand. I just try to manage it quietly. Is... is it alright that I do that, Doctor? I hope I'm not doing the wrong thing by avoiding them so much.
Has this fear of bridges caused you any significant distress or interfered with your daily life, such as missing important events or avoiding certain places altogether?

Well, I suppose... I mean, I hate to complain. I've had a very full life, you know. But... yes, I suppose it has made things a bit difficult. 

I mentioned the theater and the trips to the islands... I used to love those so much. And I had a few volunteer commitments across the water that I just... well, I had to step away from them. I told them I was just getting a bit too old for the commute, which isn't entirely untrue, but... it was really the bridges. 

My days have just gotten a bit smaller, I suppose. I stay closer to home. And I do have to rely on my children or friends to drive me if I really need to go somewhere that requires crossing over. I used to handle all of that myself, and I feel just dreadful having to ask them. I try not to ask too often, I really do. 

I hope I don't sound like I'm just feeling sorry for myself, Doctor. I know at my age, it's normal to slow down a little. Am I making too much of it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right sort of answers.

When you're not near a bridge or planning a trip, do you often find yourself worrying about future bridge crossings or feeling anxious about other things in your life, like work, health, or family matters?

Well, no, not really. I mean, I try not to be a worrier, you know? It doesn't do anyone any good to just sit around fretting all day. 

If I know I have to cross a bridge eventually, I might... well, I might think about it a little bit, just to make sure I have my plans in order so I don't inconvenience anyone. But I don't sit at home shaking in my boots about it when there's no trip planned. That would be silly, wouldn't it? 

And as for other things... well, I'm 87, Doctor. There are always little aches and pains, or things with the family to think about, but I wouldn't say I'm an anxious person overall. I try to take things as they come and count my blessings. I've had a good life, and my children are all doing well, so what is there to be terribly anxious about? 

I just try to be pleasant and not make a fuss. I hope that's the sort of answer you were looking for? I'd hate for you to think I'm just a bundle of nerves about everything. I really do try to handle things as well as I can.
